issues.description: The one-round simulation function name is inconsistent: the problem statement requires implementing `simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots:int, p: float)`, but the template defines `simulate_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float)` (while its NotImplementedError message mentions `simulate_msd_one_round`). This mismatch will cause tests/imports expecting `simulate_msd_one_round` to fail and confuses students about which function to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function `simulate_one_round` to `simulate_msd_one_round` and update its docstring/NotImplementedError text and any internal callers (e.g., `plot_msd`) to use the same name.

issues.description: The template's `inject` signature omits the type annotation for `injection_qubit` (`inject(circ, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit) -> int`), while the problem statement specifies `inject(..., injection_qubit: int) -> int`. This is a minor signature inconsistency that can confuse students about the expected parameter type (even though Python will run without the annotation).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `def inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int) -> int:` to match the problem statement (optionally also updating the docstring to clearly describe roles of data vs injection qubit).

issues.description: The meaning of the second return value from `build_msd_circ` is described inconsistently: the problem statement says it must be measurement indices for the destructive measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (in qubit order), but the template docstring describes it as indices of the final X-basis measurements of the distilled state. This can cause students to collect the wrong measurement indices/order for error detection.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template docstring for `build_msd_circ` so the second returned list is described as the measurement indices of the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (ordered by the tetrahedral qubit ordering), matching the problem statement.
